title: Repository Remote Cache Contract
description: 🌐️ The one tool-neutral description of a shared remote task cache. Every build implementation renders the same resolved contract into its own switches: Bazel into --remote_cache and friends, Nx into its self-hosted remote cache environment. The contract holds no secret: the access token is read at run time from the environment variable the contract names and is never written to disk by the repository.

Endpoint.description: Origin of the cache server: http or https, host, optional port; no credentials, path, query or fragment. HTTP is the one protocol Bazel and Nx both speak.

Instance.description: Namespace inside one server. It travels as the first URL path segment, so two repositories or two trust levels never share entries. The words the protocols use as routes are reserved.

Access.description: What the credentials of this client may do. read-only never pushes, whatever the upload switch says.

Download.description: Which outputs a build fetches from the cache: toplevel the outputs of the requested targets, all every output. Nx always fetches everything; Bazel's task adapter restores the snapshots of the requested targets from bazel-bin, so a mode that leaves them in the remote store (minimal) is not part of the contract: the restore would fail with ENOENT.

Token.description: A bearer token value: URL-safe characters only, so no shell, JSON or header quoting is ever needed.

Contract.description: The resolved contract of one enabled remote cache.

upload.description: Whether this machine pushes the results it computed locally; they only leave the machine when access is read-write too.

compression.description: Whether blobs travel compressed where the tool supports it.

Defaults.description: The committed defaults: no endpoint (the remote cache is off), read-only, and a conservative transport.

Names.description: The environment variables that override one default each; the access token variable is named by tokenEnvironment.

ServerPolicy.description: The bounds, switches and tokens of the repository's own cache server (repo remote-cache serve). The store is finite: it evicts least recently used entries beyond maximumBytes and entries idle for more than maximumAgeDays. actionResults says how far uploaded Bazel action results are checked: off, structure (a well-formed message) or complete (additionally every blob they name is stored, and a result is answered only while that holds).

directory.description: Relative to the workspace root; the default is the home the cache ledger declares for the remote cache.

readOnly.description: true refuses every write with 403, whatever token is presented.

tls.description: null serves plain HTTP; otherwise the certificate chain and private key files (PEM) of an HTTPS listener.

fleetArea.description: The area of the cache ledger (`⚡️caching/💾️storage/🧾️ledger`) where that server keeps its index: local state of the group server, never replicated, inside a partition image that the file event service does not log. The ledger resolves its directory and its budget; the server never holds more than the budget.

maintenanceSeconds.description: How often a running server re-reads its directory, so entries collected by another process stop counting; 0 switches it off.

blobSharePercent.description: The share, in percent, of the host store's cap in force that the blobs the entries reference may use (each blob once). The bound follows the cap as the cap moves with the partition; when the entries reference more, the least valuable ones leave (stale or unreached, undeclared, declared; least recently used first) down to nine tenths of it, in every staleness mode, so the rest of the cap stays for transient offload inputs and local unit outputs and the store keeps accepting writes.

blobRoom.description: What the blob bound leaves to the rest of the host store, so the store keeps accepting the next unit of the fleet instead of refusing it with a 507 (the share alone ignored the objects the unit caches hold, which nothing the cache evicts frees). headroomPercent: the share of the cap in force kept free for uploads in flight and for objects the sweep has not taken yet. floorPercent: the least the bound ever is, in percent of the cap (the cache keeps working when the unit caches fill the cap). censusMaximumSeconds: a census of the store older than this is not believed (the share alone applies). The bound is min(share, max(floor, cap - held - headroom)). / Was die Blob-Grenze dem Rest des Host-Speichers lässt, damit der Speicher die nächste Einheit der Flotte annimmt, statt sie mit 507 abzuweisen (der Anteil allein ignorierte die Objekte, die die Einheiten-Caches halten und die der Cache nicht freigeben kann). headroomPercent: Anteil der wirksamen Grenze, der für laufende Uploads und noch nicht gesammelte Objekte frei bleibt. floorPercent: das Mindeste der Grenze in Prozent (der Cache arbeitet weiter, wenn die Einheiten-Caches die Grenze füllen). censusMaximumSeconds: eine ältere Zählung des Speichers gilt nicht (es gilt der Anteil allein).

graph.description: The protected class of the graph exchange: entries that declare the kind `graph` (the head of a selection, the records of its owners) are small and take about eleven minutes and three gigabytes to produce again, and every worker needs them to become ready, so unit output pressure never takes them. sharePercent is the share, in percent, of the blob bound reserved for them (their blobs, each once, most recently used first; beyond it they compete as declared entries do); supersedeGraceSeconds is how long an entry stays after a newer entry of its slot was stored (workers that began to take the older one are not broken) before it is the first to leave.

graceSeconds.description: How long a stored entry is protected from retirement (builds in flight read it meanwhile, a registry entry no live entry consumes stays that long); 0 protects nothing.

staleness.description: How the server keeps only builds of the synchronized tree it runs on (the replica worktree of the coordinator): mode off (judge nothing), dry-run (judge, only record what would be retired or refused: counts and the first examples in GET /status, `repo remote-cache status` and `.retention/sweeps.jsonl`) or enforce (retire stale entries, refuse entries that are stale on arrival); recheckSeconds the time after which an entry that looks stale on arrival is looked at again (the replica may lag); manifestNames the files of an action result that carry the declaration of the entry; generatedRoots the first path segments that never belong to the synchronized tree; examples how many example lines a report keeps. Entries stored within graceSeconds are never retired.

Policy.description: The authored data in the build policy: which variables override the defaults, the defaults and the server bounds.

Rendering.description: What one build implementation does with the contract. Values that could carry a secret are redacted; unsupported names the contract fields the tool cannot honour.

uploadEnforcedBy.description: client: the tool itself withholds uploads. server: the tool cannot, so uploads are only prevented by a read-only token on the server. none: uploads are wanted.

Probe.description: One bounded read-only request against the path the selected tool uses; it stores nothing.

Status.description: What repo remote-cache status prints: the client contract, how both build tools render it, one probe per protocol, what the running server reports about itself and what the local store directory holds.

oneOf.description: One rendering per build backend, keyed by the backend id.

divergenceHours.description: The divergences of the running server per clock hour (UTC) and kind of output, each row with its sentence in both languages / Die Abweichungen des laufenden Servers je voller Stunde (UTC) und Art der Ausgabe, jede Zeile mit ihrem Satz in beiden Sprachen.

resolution.description: Where the endpoint and the token came from: the environment, or the fleet facts of the group store (with their generation and how the refresh ended).

instanceFrom.description: Where the instance (namespace) came from: the environment, the fleet facts (the single source of truth that the cache server publishes) or the policy default.

instanceRefused.description: The instance of the environment that the healthy fleet facts contradict and that was therefore not used (a leftover of an older provisioning); null when none.

remote.description: The truth about the server: whether it answers, whether it accepts the token on every protocol, and the entries and bytes the server itself counts (null while it does not answer a status request).

Counter.description: What one keyspace of a running server did since it started; stale counts action results dropped on a read because a blob they name left the store.

ServerStatus.description: The document a running server answers on GET /status.

blobs.description: The bytes of host store blobs the entries reference after the last collection (null before the first or without a host store), the bound they are kept within (a share of the host store's cap in force) and the bytes of blobs that left because of it.

graph.description: The protected graph class at the last collection: entries and blob bytes protected, the bytes reserved for them (null without a bound), the entries of the class that left and the blob bytes pinned for entries a newer one replaced, within the supersede grace.

evicted.description: Entries and bytes the server's retention removed since it started (age, budget, stale against the synchronized tree, dangling).

retention.description: What the last staleness sweep of the server found and what its publish gate refused since it started; absent before the first sweep or while staleness is off.

fleet.description: The fleet identities this server trusts: how many origins of the group store are usable, retired, in conflict with their pinned key, invalid or not yet registered, and how often requests were refused, by reason (never a key, a name or a secret); null while the server runs without fleet identities.

transport.description: How this server takes requests of its own group and of other groups.

divergences.description: Keys that two origins stored differently: the lifetime count, the count per class of result and the latest rows. The first entry stays, the later write was refused; both digests are evidence of nondeterminism or an attack. `advisory` counts the notes that two machines write differently by design (they are replaced, not refused); `evidence` is what the server keeps of refused writes (`GET /evidence`).

current.description: The divergences recorded since this server process started (the code it runs now; `since` is its start): what the code of today still produces. The lifetime count above also holds every divergence of code fixed since, which the history of the group keeps as evidence.

lastHour.description: The divergences of the last hour (a sliding window over the kept rows; `since` is 0).

hourly.description: The divergences per clock hour (UTC) of the last 24 hours that have any, oldest first, with the count per kind of output that differs (`stream`, `rmeta`, `rlib`, `rlib+rmeta`, …) / Die Abweichungen je voller Stunde (UTC) der letzten 24 Stunden, die welche haben, älteste zuerst, mit der Anzahl je Art der abweichenden Ausgabe.

superseded.description: Writes that replaced a different result of the same key because the newest result of that class wins (graph project records), by class; the replaced result is kept as evidence.

peers.description: What the server's read-through to peer caches did since it started.

absent.description: Peer groups configured in the topology that have no route right now (no attested endpoint, no readable store); they are never asked and count neither as a miss nor as an error.

claims.description: The fleet single-flight claim table: live claims, waiters of a long poll and the age in seconds of the oldest live claim.

consumption.description: Which origin read the action results of which origin since the server first counted: the reads in all and per `producer>consumer` pair with the compiled units among them (see the identity schema, `Consumption`).

ServerFault.description: Why the signed status request got no usable document, in place of a silent null: unreachable (no answer in time), denied (401 or 403: the signature or the role is refused), unsupported (404 or 405), failed (another HTTP status), malformed (not JSON or not a server status document). The message is in both languages.

StoreBounds.description: The finite bounds a store is opened with: total bytes, bytes per entry (not above the total) and the idle age in milliseconds after which an entry is dropped (0 keeps entries until space is needed).

Removed.description: What a collection removes, or would remove, by reason: dangling (unusable action results), stale (stale against the synchronized tree, or unreached, and the grace passed), age (idle for too long, entries that declared nothing) and budget (least valuable beyond the bound).

CollectionReport.description: What one collection of a store directory did or, for a plan, would do.

reclaimed.description: Blobs of the host store that no remaining entry references any more, and their bytes.

deferred.description: true when a running server owns the directory and retirement was left to its own collector.

GcResult.description: What repo remote-cache gc --json prints: the collection report of the directory, or a marker that the directory does not exist.

EvidenceFile.description: One file of the evidence of a refused write: the action result of one side (kept.ac, refused.ac) or one output that differs; stored is false when the blob was gone or larger than the evidence limit.

EvidenceRow.description: What the cache server keeps of one write it refused as a divergence: who, what class of result, which outputs differ, and the files that were kept (GET /evidence).

outcome.description: refused: the server serves the kept side and refused the other; superseded: the server serves the refused side, which replaced the kept one.

EvidenceList.description: What repo remote-cache evidence list prints: the evidence entries of the running server, newest first.

EvidenceDiff.description: The comparison of one output that differs: both sides (null when a side does not name the path), the first differing byte and the number of differing bytes when both sides were kept, and the lines only one side has (- kept, + refused; Brotli and JSON are unpacked), at most 20.

EvidenceShow.description: What repo remote-cache evidence show <id> prints: one evidence entry with the comparison of every output that differs.

TextCatalogue.description: The bilingual messages of the remote cache command: every key has exactly the two catalogue languages.
